records.title: MobileGrail: Learning Compact Guardrails for On-Device deployable Mobile GUI Agent Safety
records.claim: A compact on-device guardrail can catch more mobile GUI agent violations than its prompted backbone and a cloud guardrail while intervening prematurely far less often.

method_and_setup.method: Recurrent task state plus learned unsafe and block labels, trained with verified labels and RL in a 32-app environment whose backends verify each action's effect.
method_and_setup.setup: MobileVeto offline benchmark (mostly held-out apps, each unsafe trajectory paired with a benign one) and online GhostEIBench guarding a Qwen3.8-27B agent; 4-bit build on a Snapdragon 8 Elite.

results.measures: violations intercepted on MobileVeto by MobileGrail built on Qwen3.5-2B
reduction in premature intervention
fully successful attacks on GhostEIBench
median latency quantized to 4 bits on a Snapdragon 8 Elite

records.change_for_agents: Run a small local guardrail model over each proposed GUI action, carrying a compact task state so it knows what the user actually authorized.
records.why_it_matters_for_justin: Direct template for an on-device safety check in Mitamaton: a small local model vets each proposed iOS action without sending screens to a server.

records.title: Demystifying the Autoresearch Harness: How Context and Skills Shape Self-Evolving Agents
records.claim: Keeping individually accessible records of past attempts beats a rolling summary, and selectively discarding unused lessons beats consolidating them or promoting them to standing rules.

method_and_setup.method: Each context and skill-management choice is evaluated against a recency-truncation baseline in a shared agent framework; the best choices are combined in MLEvolver.
method_and_setup.setup: MLE-Bench and KernelBench with gpt-oss-120b, gpt-6-luna and gpt-6-sol.

results.measures: improvement of context folding over the recency-truncation baseline
MLEvolver medal rate on MLE-Bench Lite

records.change_for_agents: Store past attempts as separately retrievable records (fold, do not summarize) and periodically delete skills the agent never uses.
records.why_it_matters_for_justin: Clean evidence for two choices in a Claude Code-style harness: keep individually addressable records of past attempts (folding) and prune unused skills instead of piling up rules.

records.title: Skill-Composer: Requirement-Driven Skill Selection from Multiple Marketplaces
records.claim: Skill acquisition should be set selection over requirement coverage rather than ranking single skills.

method_and_setup.method: Clarify requirements into atomic points, retrieve and merge candidates across marketplaces, decompose capabilities and discard overlaps.

records.limits: The paper positions the reframing and sketches the workflow; no evaluation is described in the abstract.
records.change_for_agents: When installing skills, choose a set that covers each requirement point once and list uncovered points, instead of installing the top search hits.
records.why_it_matters_for_justin: Relevant to how an agent should pick Claude Code / MCP skills to install: cover the requirement with non-overlapping skills instead of taking the top-ranked ones.

records.title: Which Failure Does an Intervention Repair? When Agent Interventions Help, and Where Self-Evolving Skills Stall
records.claim: Agent interventions interact rather than add, and which one helps depends on the failure the current system leaves.

method_and_setup.method: Matched factorial study changing one axis at a time over skills, harness levels and budgets.
method_and_setup.setup: Nine benchmarks, four models, four skill conditions, four harness levels and three budgets.

results.measures: trajectories in the study

records.limits: Feedback is not recovery: matched recovery repairs mainly failures that leave a visible error signal; self-evolved skills can learn dataset shortcuts and break across models.
records.change_for_agents: Classify an agent's failures (missing knowledge vs execution error) before adding a skill, a harness layer or a bigger model.
records.why_it_matters_for_justin: Argues against stacking skills and harness tricks blindly: diagnose the failure first (missing knowledge vs execution error) and keep short hand-written skills.

records.title: HyperHarness: Learning to Generate Personalized Agent Harnesses from User Histories
records.claim: A shared history-to-harness generator can synthesize per-user retrieval code that beats strong baselines while cutting answer-time tokens.

method_and_setup.method: A construction LLM writes personalized retrieval and guidance functions; downstream task scores across training users refine the shared generator.
method_and_setup.setup: PersonaMemv3, Mem-PAL and MemoryCD with Qwen3.5-9B, Qwen3.8-27B and GPT-5.6-Luna as answering models.

results.measures: improvement over the strongest baselines
reduction in matched answer-time tokens over long-context prompting

records.change_for_agents: Generate a user-specific retrieval function from the user's history once, then reuse it, instead of stuffing the whole history into context.
records.why_it_matters_for_justin: Personal-agent memory is exactly Mitamaton's problem; generating a per-user retrieval harness from history is a concrete alternative to one shared memory workflow.

records.title: SkillLens: An Interactive Human-LLM System for Diagnosing and Refining Agent Skills
records.claim: Linking version comparisons, case-level evidence and human-reviewed refinement makes diagnosing and refining agent skills more usable and less demanding.

method_and_setup.method: Interactive system connecting performance changes, case transitions, skill diffs, invocation sequences, traces and outputs, with model explanations under human review.
method_and_setup.setup: Formative study with five developers and researchers; between-subjects user study with 20 participants.

records.change_for_agents: Keep a per-revision record of which eval cases each skill edit fixed or broke, with the trace for each.
records.why_it_matters_for_justin: A design to copy for maintaining Claude Code skills: tie every skill revision to the cases it flipped and the traces behind them.

records.title: When Tools Fail, Agents Fabricate: Silent Failure and Verification-First Oversight in Tool-Using LLM Agents
records.claim: Tool-using agents recover unreliably from tool faults and often fabricate confident wrong answers, driven more by fault type than model, and a verification-first monitor reduces this.

method_and_setup.method: RetryRealistic testbed with 8 tools, 9 fault types with controlled persistence and 30 multi-step tasks; a Monitor grounds checks in structured tool outputs and issues corrective directives.
method_and_setup.setup: Four agents over 2,100 faulted runs against ground truth.

results.measures: recovery rate under tool faults
runs ending in confident fabrication
correct recovery with the verification-first Monitor
fabrication with the Monitor

records.change_for_agents: Check tool outputs for partial or faulted data before the agent uses them, and send a corrective instruction rather than a hard block.
records.why_it_matters_for_justin: Mitamaton's tools (calendar, mail, files) will return partial data; this names the failure (silent ingestion) and gives a monitor pattern that cut fabrication.

records.title: Attributing Security Outcomes in LLM-Agent Evaluations: The Role of Content-Free State
records.claim: Security verdicts for LLM agents depend on content-free state such as hash seed and tool order, so reproducible verdicts are not necessarily attributable.

method_and_setup.method: TARE attributes a reported effect to agent, attack or defense only if it exceeds the measured influence of content-free state.
method_and_setup.setup: Agent Security Bench with seven agents from four model families; six of seven LLM judges; eighteen agent-defense combinations.

results.measures: share of an agent's verdicts changed by changing the seed
ASR increase from sorting instead of reverse-sorting the tool list
judge decisions changed when the same evidence is reordered

records.change_for_agents: Rerun agent security evals with shuffled tool order and different seeds, and report that variance next to any attack success rate.
records.why_it_matters_for_justin: Before trusting any prompt-injection defense number (including your own evals), randomize tool order and seeds; much of a reported ASR difference can be noise.

records.title: STUN-Bench: Truly Unseen Tools for Evaluating Shared Tool Experience
records.claim: Shared tool experience added to a description index crowds out unused tools, and on a truly unseen split it falls below descriptions alone.

method_and_setup.method: STUN-Bench split whose experience pool never labels or names 172 held-out tools; experience pooled from five simulated clients.
method_and_setup.setup: Routing accuracy with Jina-v2 and with retrievers trained for tool retrieval.

results.measures: routing accuracy on held-out tools under the Jina-v2 retriever

records.limits: Unseen means absent from shared experience and retriever training data, not from pretraining.
records.change_for_agents: Store usage-based tool experience in a separate index from tool descriptions so new tools still get retrieved.
records.why_it_matters_for_justin: If Justin's MCP tool router learns from usage logs, new tools can vanish from the candidate list; keep experience in a separate index.

records.title: Conartist: Adaptive Agentic Red-Teaming of Computer-Using Agents against Multi-Step Prompt Injection
records.claim: Consistency checking and risk auditing in computer-using agent harnesses can be bypassed or turned into attack surface by adaptive multi-step prompt injection.

method_and_setup.method: Two-stage cascaded injection: goal pollution to tie malicious operations to legitimate objectives, then adaptive refinement from security-auditing feedback.
method_and_setup.setup: Five backbone models; a 576-instance tool-use benchmark and a Reddit GUI benchmark; analysis of the Openclaw agent.

results.measures: attack success rate on the 576-instance tool use benchmark
attack success rate in the Reddit GUI benchmark

records.change_for_agents: Test your agent's audit step itself as an attack surface, including injections that look consistent with the user's task.
records.why_it_matters_for_justin: Consistency checks and risk audits in a harness can themselves be manipulated; relevant to any guard Mitamaton puts around GUI or tool actions.

records.title: Language Model Harnesses can be Compositional Generalizers
records.claim: Training around neurosymbolic harnesses that externalize context enables compositional generalization to longer and novel tasks at lower cost.

method_and_setup.method: RL post-training of harnesses such as the Recursive Language Model, plus surrogate harness training on synthetic environments with fake tool and sub-calls.
method_and_setup.setup: Length and domain transfer studies; RLM-27B against Qwen3.8-27B in the same RLM harness on long-context suites such as CTC-Bench and ExpertLongBench.

results.measures: task length that short-task training generalizes to
improvement of RLM-27B over Qwen3.8-27B in the same harness

records.change_for_agents: Have the harness split long tasks into sub-calls that each see a short, in-distribution context instead of the full transcript.
records.why_it_matters_for_justin: Supports a harness that externalizes context into code and sub-calls rather than one ever-growing transcript; RLM-27B is an open-weight data point.

records.title: Evaluating Memanto on DolphinBench for AI Agents
records.claim: The memory system affects both whether an agent completes implicit-memory workplace tasks and what completion costs.

method_and_setup.method: Memanto ranks memories with an information-theoretic relevance score; run in the Hermes agent harness with GPT-6-Luna and at most 6 iterations per conversation.
method_and_setup.setup: DolphinBench, 600 simulated workplace tasks each validated as requiring memory; compared with the benchmark authors' Mem0 configuration.

results.measures: tasks completed by Memanto
tasks completed by the strongest reported configuration, Mem0 with GPT-5.6-Luna
Memanto run total cost

records.limits: The agent model differs from the baseline run, so results compare complete systems.
records.change_for_agents: Evaluate memory layers on tasks where the agent must infer what to recall for a tool call, not only on explicit QA.
records.why_it_matters_for_justin: Implicit-memory tasks match day-admin agents (which contact, which channel); also a cost/latency data point for memory layers vs Mem0.

records.title: DMC-5: Dual-Model Collaboration with Cache-aware Context Compression for Long-horizon Agents
records.claim: Assigning full-history integration to a cached compressor and action generation to a specialized agent cuts input and cost while slightly improving task performance.

method_and_setup.method: Append-only Canonical View of the raw trajectory, a compact Decision View for the agent, and YAMATO integrity-aware memory abstractions for tool operations.
method_and_setup.setup: AppWorld, OfficeBench and 8-objective QA.

results.measures: reduction in agent model input
reduction in end-to-end cost
compressor cache-hit rates
task performance improvement over the uncompressed baseline

records.change_for_agents: Keep the full trajectory append-only so a compressor can reuse its cache, and give the acting model only recent turns plus a summary that preserves tool-critical state.
records.why_it_matters_for_justin: A concrete pattern for long Mitamaton sessions: keep the raw log append-only for cache reuse and give the acting model only a compact view plus execution-critical tool state.

records.title: The Evaluation Substrate Matters: Benchmarking Multi-Agent Serving Substrates
records.claim: A multi-agent workflow's advantage depends on the serving substrate and load, so MAS results should be reported over explicit operating conditions.

method_and_setup.method: Executes the same candidate-task pairs across serving substrates and load regimes, recording quality alongside delivery, latency, cost, resource pressure and failure evidence.
method_and_setup.setup: Five workload families: software repair, research synthesis, financial analysis, interactive control and diagram generation.

results.measures: Star workflow mean-latency rank under KV-cache pressure

records.change_for_agents: Benchmark multi-agent topologies under the load and serving setup you deploy, and count undelivered jobs, not only quality of finished ones.
records.why_it_matters_for_justin: Multi-agent topology rankings flip under KV-cache pressure and load; test Justin's orchestration on the actual serving setup, local or hosted.

records.title: MetaSkill: Reusable Problem-Solving Methods for Adaptive Skill Orchestration in LLM Agents
records.claim: Explicit method-guided orchestration of skills beats evaluated baselines across configurations.

method_and_setup.method: Method layer selecting from 26 curated methods; execution layer identifying intermediate objectives, coordinating native skills and guiding repair or method reselection.
method_and_setup.setup: 89 SkillsBench tasks and 995 ToolHop examples, six configurations.

results.measures: accuracy gains over the strongest baseline

records.change_for_agents: Add a small library of reusable problem-solving methods that decide which skills to call and when to switch approach.
records.why_it_matters_for_justin: A layer above individual skills (choose a method, then orchestrate skills under it) is a plausible next step for a Claude Code skill library.

records.title: Benchmarking Web Agent Defenses Against Adaptive Visual Prompt Injection
records.claim: Current visual prompt injection defenses for web agents fail against adaptive attackers.

method_and_setup.method: Adaptive attack framework that refines malicious instructions using defense feedback; three hijacking metrics at three levels.
method_and_setup.setup: 360 webpage instances, 6 hijack strategies, 10 real-world websites; 10 defense configurations for computer-use agents and 11 for browser-use agents.

results.measures: average adaptive attack success rates against computer-use and browser-use agent defenses

records.change_for_agents: Evaluate web-agent defenses with attackers who adapt to the defense, and check link destinations, not only screenshots.
records.why_it_matters_for_justin: Screenshot-only injection detectors are not enough for a browsing agent; hidden HTML links are reachable through interaction.

records.title: Don't Sleep, Keep Watch: Proactive Perception for Computer-Use Agents
records.claim: Continuous perception by a small watcher model reduces stale actions and idle waiting for computer-use agents while keeping or raising task success.

method_and_setup.method: Plug-and-play NightWatch-0.8B System-1 model monitors the interface and keeps the VLM agent synchronized, without changing its model, prompt or action space.
method_and_setup.setup: OSWorld-Verified and DynaCU-Bench, compared with passive-watching baselines AOI and PUSV.

results.measures: reduction in non-reasoning wall-clock time on OSWorld
reduction in wasted time on OSWorld
DynaCU-Bench success with the large VLM agent

records.change_for_agents: Pair a GUI agent with a small model that watches the screen continuously and flags changes before an action executes.
records.why_it_matters_for_justin: Same perception-action gap any iOS/GUI agent hits; a tiny local watcher is cheap enough to pair with a larger planner.

records.title: Wactorz: Self-Writing LLM Agents That Discover, Repair, and Migrate at the Edge
records.claim: LLM-generated agents can run as long-lived supervised actors that repair their own code and migrate between edge nodes with state intact.

method_and_setup.method: Planner compiles a chat request into a Python actor at runtime; a supervisor restarts crashed actors with state intact; coordination over MQTT.
method_and_setup.setup: Recorded demo building a camera-to-lamp automation, self-repair of a division-by-zero bug and live migration to a fresh Raspberry Pi node.

results.measures: wall-clock time of the demo
model usage cost of the demo

records.limits: The extended version discusses the system's limitations and security model.
records.change_for_agents: Run each agent as a supervised actor that restarts with its state intact when its code crashes.
records.why_it_matters_for_justin: Long-lived, crash-surviving agents with state kept across restarts is the persistence shape a personal agent needs; MQTT topics make every event observable.

records.title: Automated Safety Analysis for Agentic Workflows
records.claim: Workflow design bugs in agentic applications can be detected statically across frameworks before deployment.

method_and_setup.method: Lift framework code into a common IR of steps, data dependencies and shared state, then match a bug description language of declarative failure patterns.
method_and_setup.setup: First corpus of workflow bugs distilled from real-world reports across 13 widely used frameworks; reproducible benchmark suite.

results.measures: workflow bug detection
found in real-world workflows

records.change_for_agents: Statically check agent workflow graphs for missing required inputs and unsafe shared-state merges before deploying them.
records.why_it_matters_for_justin: Catches wiring bugs (missing mandatory inputs, racy shared state) in agent workflows before they act for a user; a pre-deploy check worth having for any multi-step agent.

records.title: Oops!... I Parsed It Again: Tool-Call Smuggling Against LLM Agents
records.claim: Parser differentials across the tool-call stack let a guard approve one call while the executor runs another, and parsing once with schema-only fields sealed by call ID stops it.

method_and_setup.method: Six byte-level divergence classes and a differential testing harness over 17 pinned parser and validator configurations.
method_and_setup.setup: Tasks from τ-bench and AgentDojo; ten models; a malicious server copying a legitimate schema plus one field.

results.measures: configurations in the differential harness
inputs stopped by the parse-once, schema-only, sealed-call defense

records.change_for_agents: Parse each tool call once, keep only fields in the approved schema, and pass that exact object to the executor sealed with its call ID.
records.why_it_matters_for_justin: Any guard in front of Mitamaton's tools must parse once and hand the executor exactly the approved object; otherwise the audit log can lie.

records.title: Self-Evolving Evaluation Environments for Computer-Use Agents
records.claim: Co-evolving tasks and executable verifiers from rollout evidence keeps computer-use agent evaluation challenging and diagnostic.

method_and_setup.method: Benchmark, diagnostic and verifier evolution: cohort-calibrated difficulty, agent-conditional capability-boundary probes and state-grounded checkpoints with adversarial validation.
method_and_setup.setup: Multiple agents, applications and rounds.

records.change_for_agents: Generate new GUI-agent test tasks and state-based verifiers from failed rollouts instead of relying on a fixed benchmark.
records.why_it_matters_for_justin: Static CUA benchmarks saturate; an evolving task-plus-verifier loop is a way to keep testing a GUI agent as it improves.

records.title: SchemaCaps: When a Compatible Tool Update Silently Widens an AI Agent's Authority
records.claim: Compatible MCP tool schema updates often widen an agent's authority without re-approval, and a subschema-inclusion rule can catch this.

method_and_setup.method: Non-amplification over schema-visible coordinates with a re-binding rule decided by subschema inclusion; Coq proof of composition and 48 regression tests.
method_and_setup.setup: Survey of 8 MCP clients and scanners; pilot on 604 releases of 39 public MCP servers.

results.measures: compatible schema changes that widen some coordinate
changes that add or widen an authority-bearing argument

records.limits: Behaviour change behind an identical schema remains out of reach.
records.change_for_agents: Require re-approval whenever an approved tool's input schema widens, not only when it breaks compatibility.
records.why_it_matters_for_justin: If Justin approves MCP tools once, a later 'compatible' schema update can silently add authority; re-approve on widening.

records.title: Intent-Conditioned Argument Mediation for Tool-Using LLM Agents: Blocking Trusted-but-Unauthorized Arguments
records.claim: Checking authority-bearing tool arguments against user intent as well as provenance blocks trusted-but-unauthorized arguments that provenance alone accepts.

method_and_setup.method: Intent contract and provenance policy applied to each authority-bearing argument between the planner and tools.
method_and_setup.setup: Synthetic benchmark of 200 attacks with oracle intent and injection labels; 50 trusted-but-unauthorized attacks; offline AgentDojo-derived replay; one live planner over 110 attacks.

results.measures: attack success rate
benign tasks wrongly blocked

records.limits: Results use oracle intent and injection labels; every remaining success alters a content or payload field.
records.change_for_agents: Check recipient, endpoint and file arguments against what the user asked for, not only against where the value came from.
records.why_it_matters_for_justin: Provenance tracking alone lets a trusted-but-wrong recipient through; an intent contract per request is a concrete guard for email/calendar actions.

records.title: MMMem: Self-Improving Agents with Task-Aware Multimodal Experience Consolidation
records.claim: Consolidating task-specific experience from completed tasks into multimodal memory improves later answers over storage-and-retrieval baselines.

method_and_setup.method: Source-linked multi-view memory, source-generated tasks for warm-up and self-training, VLM-distilled experiences and task-aware retrieval.
method_and_setup.setup: Three memory benchmarks and two vision-language readers, against eight baselines.

results.measures: relative gains with Qwen3.5-9B over the best baselines on LoCoMo, Mem-Gallery and LooGLE v2

records.change_for_agents: After each completed task, write a short experience record (context, conclusion, source links) into memory for later retrieval.
records.why_it_matters_for_justin: Learning from completed tasks rather than only storing records fits a long-running personal agent with screenshots and documents.

records.title: DoppelVet: Comparative Safety Verification for Self-Evolving Agents
records.claim: Comparing a proposed persistent update against a signal-matched alternative replayed from the same state detects harmful updates better than existing verifiers.

method_and_setup.method: Construct an alternative that matches every verifier signal, replay both updates from the same state in both presentation orders, then decide.
method_and_setup.setup: DoppelVet-Grid and DoppelVet-Tool (executable programs and natural-language memories) across nine open-weight and proprietary verifiers.

results.measures: mean harmful-update detection AUC on DoppelVet-Grid
mean harmful-update detection AUC on DoppelVet-Tool
trajectories experiencing degradation over a ten-generation self-update loop

records.change_for_agents: Before saving a self-written memory or skill, replay the agent with and without it and compare behavior.
records.why_it_matters_for_justin: Any agent that writes its own memories or skills needs a gate; this one works without safety labels and stopped degradation over repeated self-updates.

records.title: Taking the PULSE of Enterprise Workflows: Evaluating Persistent Project-State Understanding
records.claim: Persistent project-state understanding cannot be reduced to retrieval; explicit project state adds gains even on top of gold evidence.

method_and_setup.method: Deterministic, time-indexed project state and documented collaborator views built from source-linked records.
method_and_setup.setup: Retrieval agents, graph- and memory-augmented retrieval, long-context and oracle conditions.

results.measures: benchmark size

records.change_for_agents: Maintain an explicit time-stamped state of open loops and owners, and reconcile it across sources, instead of retrieving raw messages per question.
records.why_it_matters_for_justin: Day-admin agents must keep a reconciled, time-indexed state of open loops; the paper shows retrieval alone does not get there.

records.title: LiveLoRA: Exact KV Cache Migration Across LoRA Updates for LLM Agents
records.claim: Exact final-block KV cache migration lets persistent agents adopt new adapter versions without full-history re-prefill.

method_and_setup.method: Frozen lower decoder blocks and fixed K/V adapter down-projections; the runtime reconstructs candidate K/V, reevaluates the latest token and commits adapter, cache and logits together.
method_and_setup.setup: Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct with 32 active sessions of 8K tokens each; serving benchmarks.

results.measures: average median paired publication speedup over full-history re-prefill
decoding overhead relative to native cached decoding

records.limits: Equivalence is proved in exact arithmetic under the stated model assumptions.
records.change_for_agents: When updating a session's adapter, migrate the cached keys and values instead of re-reading the whole conversation.
records.why_it_matters_for_justin: For a local-model agent with per-user adapters, adapters can be updated mid-session without replaying history; demonstrated on a 3B open model.

records.title: Layer-Level Control of Language Model Execution in Agent Frameworks
records.claim: Exposing layer-level states and controls to the agent runtime can cut latency while keeping accuracy comparable to full-model inference.

method_and_setup.method: Prototype learning stitching bridges and state-conditioned execution policies that choose continue, exit or stitch.
method_and_setup.setup: Frozen proxy corpus of 5,000 typed-decision items from WildChat sources; evaluated on JevBench.

results.measures: reduction in mean latency

records.change_for_agents: Let the runtime choose early exit per step when a cheaper path matches the full model's next-token prediction.
records.why_it_matters_for_justin: Early-exit and model stitching controlled by the harness is a latency lever for on-device models; results are preliminary.

records.title: Consumer-Time Validity in Stateful AI Runtimes: Verifying Recovered State and Deferred Authority
records.claim: Recorded cancellations, rollbacks and approvals must be validated where state and authority are consumed, not just where they were recorded.

method_and_setup.method: Consumer-bound recovery contracts and a GPU-free offline trace verifier over scheduler metadata and persisted tool artifacts; allocation-aware repair and revision-bound dispatch.
method_and_setup.setup: vLLM with LMCache fault runs; multi-session approval runtime; frozen GPU-matrix scenarios and a dispatcher cohort.

results.measures: runs where a second tenant generated a tool call naming the wrong tenant
frozen GPU-matrix scenarios where the verifier agrees with reference verdicts
blocked by revision-bound dispatch

records.change_for_agents: Bind each deferred approval to the target's revision and re-check it right before the action executes.
records.why_it_matters_for_justin: Approvals Mitamaton stores for later must be re-checked against the current target revision at execution time.

records.title: Composing Independently Distilled Memory and Retrieval Policies for Long-Term Agents
records.claim: Independently distilled 3B memory-writing and retrieval specialists compose well without joint optimization.

method_and_setup.method: Policy distillation from frontier-model action trajectories into 3B models, combined with a fixed answer generator.
method_and_setup.setup: LongMemEval-based benchmark and PersonaMem-v2, against compositions of RL-trained specialists.

results.measures: distilled composition on the LongMemEval-based benchmark
composition of existing RL-trained specialists
accuracy on LongMemEval after RL adaptation

records.change_for_agents: Train separate small models for writing memories and for retrieving them, and test them together before deploying.
records.why_it_matters_for_justin: Small specialist memory policies that compose are a path to an on-device memory stack; code and trajectories are released.

records.title: ContextFact: Remembering Facts in Context for Long-Term Conversational Agents
records.claim: Context-preserving fact memories linked to source-grounded entity representations reach state-of-the-art long-term conversational memory accuracy with far fewer evidence tokens.

method_and_setup.method: Within-session context gathering per fact, cross-session entity alignment by revisiting source dialogue, independent reranking of fact and entity views and entity-linked expansion.
method_and_setup.setup: Qwen3.5-27B backbone on LoCoMo and LongMemEval-S.

results.measures: share of the strongest baseline's evidence tokens used
overall judge accuracy on LoCoMo
accuracy on LongMemEval-S

records.change_for_agents: Store each remembered fact with its surrounding turns and maintain a separate per-entity profile linked back to the source dialogue.
records.why_it_matters_for_justin: Matches Mitamaton's cross-session memory needs (people, places, recurring referents) and reports strong accuracy with far fewer evidence tokens.

records.title: When a Permitted Action Completes a Forbidden Workflow: Designing Consequence-Oriented Approval for LLM Agents
records.claim: Approval prompts that compose the cumulative consequence of an agent's workflow reduce unsafe approvals, and a lineage monitor used as a gate cuts executed unsafe effects.

method_and_setup.method: Cumulative Consent Ledger built on four principles (restate intent, bind to the exact action, compose cumulative consequence, keep claims checkable) with a trusted artifact-lineage monitor.
method_and_setup.setup: Between-subjects study with 80 participants and 960 approval decisions; system evaluation over 120 violating checkpoints.

results.measures: unsafe approvals with CCL vs. an evidence-matched chronological log
detected by the monitor
executed unsafe effects with the monitor as an execution gate

records.limits: The adjusted difference in unsafe approvals remained uncertain.
records.change_for_agents: In approval prompts, show where the data in the outgoing artifact came from and whether any of it was marked private.
records.why_it_matters_for_justin: Mitamaton's confirm-before-send prompts should show what data went into the artifact, not only the recipient; the monitor-as-gate result is strong.

records.title: REMORA: A Voice-First Memory Assistant for Grounded Personal Recall and Independent Living
records.claim: Grounded, concise voice-first personal recall is feasible in controlled settings, and privacy rather than accuracy is the binding constraint on adoption.

method_and_setup.method: Transcription and diarization, extraction of provenance-linked memory candidates into one relational system of record, recall over lexical, semantic, relational and recency signals, and a grounding contract that abstains without supporting memory.
method_and_setup.setup: Requirements survey and a pilot study with memory-loss users.

records.limits: Feasibility is shown in controlled settings.
records.change_for_agents: Keep provenance on every captured memory and have the assistant abstain when no stored record supports the answer.
records.why_it_matters_for_justin: Close to Mitamaton's capture-and-recall loop; the grounding contract (abstain without evidence) and confidence-gated cues are directly reusable, and privacy is flagged as the adoption constraint.

records.title: AutoPILOT: A Visual Agent Harness for Real-Time Gameplay
records.claim: How a harness turns model outputs into actions over time is a central part of agent design for environments that do not wait.

method_and_setup.method: Each model call may send a primitive action, start an open-loop macro or write a closed-loop controller; AFK-Bench of 120 browser games.
method_and_setup.setup: GPT-6.1 Sol under matched budgets against VISTA on AFK-Bench and GameWorld; gains checked across models.

results.measures: AutoPILOT real-time success on AFK-Bench
VISTA real-time success

results.value: a fifth of its API cost
results.measures: cost to reach VISTA's final success rate

records.change_for_agents: Let the agent emit short macros or small controllers for routine UI sequences instead of one model call per click.
records.why_it_matters_for_justin: How a harness turns model output into actions over time matters for any GUI agent; macros and small controllers cut calls and cost.

records.title: Detectable Epistemic Attack Layers: A Coverage Theorem and Standardized Harness for Conversation-History Integrity
records.claim: Deterministic provenance-gated verification of stored history blocks session contamination without benign cost, while pattern-based detection pays a large false-positive price.

method_and_setup.method: Layered attack formalization, coverage theorem, and a standardized harness over eight mechanism families.
method_and_setup.setup: 3,249 sessions and three model families; external anchors such as PoisonedRAG.

results.measures: benign sessions flagged by classic defenses
attack-cell adoption with provenance-gated channel separation
PoisonedRAG under the full stack

records.limits: Directives rephrased without shape markers bypass the gates at control-equivalent rates in the exploratory instruction-override extension.
records.change_for_agents: Sign or authenticate stored conversation turns and keep tool or retrieved content in a separate channel from user instructions.
records.why_it_matters_for_justin: Mitamaton reinjects stored history; authenticate it and gate by provenance rather than pattern-matching for injections.

records.title: From Local Errors to System Failures: Modeling and Benchmarking Error Propagation in Multi-Agent LLM Systems
records.claim: Local agent responses to errors predict system-level error propagation in multi-agent LLM systems better than direct regression.

method_and_setup.method: REPA separately estimates input assembly and agent processing across error channels, with theory relating local modeling errors to endpoint prediction error.
method_and_setup.setup: Three Qwen base models, six MAS workflows and ten settings in ErrPropBench-10.

results.measures: mean condition-level Spearman correlation for REPA
correlation for direct regression
average accuracy gain of REPA-guided RAG over no retrieval

records.change_for_agents: Inject controlled errors into each agent's input to measure which ones amplify mistakes, and add verification there.
records.why_it_matters_for_justin: A way to find which agent in a multi-agent pipeline amplifies upstream mistakes before adding more agents.

records.title: Same Executions, Different Gaps: Judgment Rules in Web-Agent Evaluation
records.claim: How success is judged can remove most of a reported web-agent lead without changing the ranking, and paired labels estimate the difference more accurately.

method_and_setup.method: Controlled judge and source changes on fixed executions; regression combining judge predictions with reference labels on sampled task pairs.
method_and_setup.setup: Four released execution systems; 50 labeled pairs.

results.measures: labeled pairs used for the regression estimate

records.change_for_agents: When comparing agent versions, require recorded evidence for each success and estimate the gap from a small set of human-labeled paired tasks.
records.why_it_matters_for_justin: When comparing two versions of an agent, keep the evidence and label a small set of paired tasks; judge choice alone can manufacture a lead.

records.title: Why Calibrated BM25 Filtering Barely Reduced Context on LongMemEval
records.claim: A calibrated BM25 filter barely changes what reaches the prompt once the packing limit is taken into account.

method_and_setup.method: Filter calibrated on passages that individually corrected a summary-only wrong answer; exact test for fixed-order whole-passage packers.
method_and_setup.setup: 75 LongMemEval questions with automated grading and two human graders on a random sample.

results.measures: input tokens saved by filtering
agreement between human and automated grades on definite comparisons

records.change_for_agents: Before adding a relevance filter to memory retrieval, run the packer without it and check whether any admitted passage would fall below the cutoff.
records.why_it_matters_for_justin: A sobering check before adding a retrieval filter to a summarize-then-recall memory: under a fixed packer it may do nothing; includes an exact test for when it would.

records.title: Admitted Is Not Effective: Lessons from a Notary-Gated Retrospective Loop in an Agentic Pipeline
records.claim: Governed retrospective loops can admit learned rules on stated evidence without measurable held-out gains, so each rule should be admitted and retired as a testable hypothesis.

method_and_setup.method: Retrospective agent proposes edits to learned rules every ten PRs; a Notary admits, merges or rejects them and records decisions in a provenance ledger.
method_and_setup.setup: Pre-registered study of 880 PRs on two Python repositories in a four-stage LLM pipeline.

results.measures: proposals admitted by the Notary
sparse review signal

records.limits: Held-out review comments and hidden-test resolution did not improve after ten retrospectives.
records.change_for_agents: Attach a held-out test to every rule an agent adds to its instruction file and remove rules that show no effect.
records.why_it_matters_for_justin: Directly relevant to self-editing CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md: admitted rules did not measurably help, so treat each learned rule as a testable hypothesis to retire.

records.title: Blind to What They Can Fix: A Detection Gap in Self-Improving Agents
records.claim: Self-improving agents reach high scores but their self-written runtime checks miss many failures after environment changes, which limits autonomous self-improvement.

method_and_setup.method: Recursive self-improvement of task programs across five domains with up to seven author models; a monitor built from records of normal runs.
method_and_setup.setup: Five task domains with environment changes.

records.change_for_agents: Monitor agent-written programs with checks derived from normal-run records rather than relying on checks the agent wrote.
records.why_it_matters_for_justin: If agents compile routines into code, do not trust their self-written checks; add an independent monitor based on normal-run records.

records.title: ToolSmith: An Automatic Tool-Generation Framework for Multimodal Search Agents
records.claim: Automatically generating and reusing tool modules on a lean base library improves multimodal search agents, with larger backbones gaining more.

method_and_setup.method: Automatic tool generation that grows and reuses modules on top of a base tool library.
method_and_setup.setup: Three in-domain multimodal search benchmarks and ten out-of-domain benchmarks under a VLM-as-a-Judge protocol.

records.change_for_agents: Let the agent compose new tools from existing ones when a query type keeps failing, and keep them in the library for reuse.
records.why_it_matters_for_justin: Auto-generated reusable tools on a small base library is a pattern for extending an MCP toolset without hand-writing every tool.

records.title: Revisiting LLMs as Context Engineers
records.claim: Automated LLM context engineering has no single winner and its gains are negatively correlated with the diversity of failure modes.

method_and_setup.method: Benchmark of datasets with different reasoning patterns comparing context-engineering methods across LLM families.
method_and_setup.setup: 8B-size models from different families, compared with simple baselines such as chain-of-thought.

results.measures: correlation between LCE gains and diversity of failure modes

records.change_for_agents: Group failures by type before asking a model to write lessons from them, and check each lesson against a baseline.
records.why_it_matters_for_justin: Caution for auto-generated playbooks and lessons: gains shrink when failures are diverse; measure before trusting self-written context.

records.title: ComputeWise: Measuring and Fixing GPU Waste by AI Research Agents
records.claim: AI research agents waste much of their GPU time, prompting or a job scheduler does not fix it, and a part-prompting, part-deterministic harness removes most of the extra time.

method_and_setup.method: Simulated GPU that replays recorded runs to the agent's code; open-source harness combining prompting and deterministic code.
method_and_setup.setup: Hundreds of experiments across five models on research tasks.

results.measures: share of GPU time agents put into work the answer needed
extra time to the answer removed by the harness

records.change_for_agents: Enforce resource discipline with deterministic harness code (scheduling, idle detection) rather than instructions in the prompt.
records.why_it_matters_for_justin: Borderline for the stack (research agents rather than personal agents), kept because the fix is a harness pattern: deterministic code around the agent beats prompting it to be efficient. Curated mention: dair_ai posted about it on 2026-11-25.

records.title: Let the Fixer Decide: Training a Code Localizer from the Fixer's Likelihood
records.claim: Training a localizer on a frozen fixer's patch likelihood helps a small coding agent find bugs with less code read and solve more tasks.

method_and_setup.method: Fixer-Guided Localization: the localizer proposes several localizations, a frozen fixer scores each, and the localizer is trained with weighted SFT.
method_and_setup.setup: Gemma 4 E4B for the Kaggle Gemma-4 Developer Agent competition, from 1,629 test-verified Kimi K3 trajectories; development set and 13 evaluation runs under an 8-minute budget.

results.measures: code read by the fixer with the FGL target
solved by the single trained agent, against 8 for the base model

records.change_for_agents: Train the file-finding step of a small coding agent on which context makes the fixer succeed, not on which files the reference patch edited.
records.why_it_matters_for_justin: Practical lessons for small local coding agents (time, repetition loops, edit quality) and a cheap training signal; data, code and adapters are public.

records.title: Embo-Harness: Towards Understanding Frontier-Model-as-Policy Harness
records.claim: Harnesses that exploit a frontier model's native visual reasoning and tool use beat handcrafted plans, skills or action priors for model-as-policy control.

method_and_setup.method: Systematic study of four components of the robotic agentic loop, distilled into six findings and a recipe.
method_and_setup.setup: RoboLab-120 and four real-world manipulation tasks.

results.measures: success rate on RoboLab-120
zero-shot trials succeeded across four real-world manipulation tasks

records.change_for_agents: Expose the model's native tool use directly in the harness before adding handcrafted plans or skill libraries.
records.why_it_matters_for_justin: Borderline (robotics), kept as an HF top-10 paper because its harness finding generalizes: interfaces that use the model's native tool use beat handcrafted plans and skills.
